description: Lamb Ouzi is a magnificent Middle Eastern dish featuring a whole slow roasted lamb, traditionally stuffed with aromatic spiced rice, nuts, and tender meat. This celebratory meal is a true showstopper, offering incredibly tender lamb infused with rich flavors. Prepare for a feast that will transport your taste buds straight to the heart of the Middle East.

ingredients.notes: bone-in, butterflied or deboned for stuffing

instructions.title: Prepare and Marinate the Lamb
instructions.text: Pat the lamb dry. In a small bowl, combine 2 tablespoons of baharat, 1 teaspoon of salt, and 1 teaspoon of black pepper. Rub this spice mixture generously all over the lamb, ensuring it gets into all crevices. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to penetrate.

instructions.title: Prepare the Spiced Rice Stuffing
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil and 2 tablespoons of ghee in a large pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon of baharat, cinnamon, and cardamom. Add the soaked and drained basmati rice, stirring to coat with the spices. Pour in 2 cups of lamb or chicken broth and season with salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is partially cooked. Fluff with a fork and let cool slightly.

instructions.title: Stuff and Truss the Lamb
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 325F (160C). Lay the marinated lamb flat, skin-side down. Evenly spread the partially cooked spiced rice stuffing over the lamb, leaving a border around the edges. Carefully roll or fold the lamb to enclose the stuffing. Secure the lamb with kitchen twine, tying it at intervals to keep its shape and seal in the stuffing. Place the stuffed lamb in a large roasting pan.

instructions.title: Slow Roast the Lamb to Perfection
instructions.text: Pour 2 cups of lamb or chicken broth into the bottom of the roasting pan. Cover the pan tightly with foil. Roast in the preheated oven for 3 to 4 hours, or until the lamb is fork-tender. The internal temperature should reach 145F (63C) for medium-rare, or higher for more well-done. For the last 30 minutes, remove the foil to allow the lamb to brown and crisp up. Baste occasionally with the pan juices.

instructions.title: Prepare Garnish and Rest the Lamb
instructions.text: While the lamb rests, in a small pan, toast the pine nuts and blanched almonds in a dry pan over medium heat until golden brown and fragrant. Be careful not to burn them. Once roasted, carefully remove the lamb from the pan and let it rest on a cutting board, tented with foil, for at least 20 minutes before carving. This allows the juices to redistribute.

instructions.title: Serve the Magnificent Lamb Ouzi
instructions.text: Carve the slow roasted lamb into thick slices, ensuring each slice includes some of the flavorful rice stuffing. Arrange the lamb on a large serving platter. Drizzle with any remaining pan juices. Garnish generously with the toasted pine nuts, almonds, and fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately as the centerpiece of your Middle Eastern feast, often accompanied by yogurt sauce or a simple salad.

tips: For an even deeper flavor, marinate the lamb for 24 hours. You can also make small incisions in the lamb and stuff with garlic slivers before marinating.
If you dont have baharat spice blend, you can make your own with equal parts ground cumin, coriander, paprika, and black pepper, plus a pinch of cloves and nutmeg.
Serve Lamb Ouzi with a side of cool labneh (strained yogurt), a fresh cucumber and tomato salad, or a sprinkle of pomegranate seeds for a burst of color and tang.
article:
Experience the culinary majesty of the Middle East right in your home with a show-stopping dish that embodies celebration and exquisite flavor: Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi. More than just a meal, Lamb Ouzi is an event, a centerpiece that transforms any gathering into an unforgettable feast. Imagine a succulent, fall-off-the-bone lamb, slow-roasted to perfection, infused with aromatic spices, and served alongside a fragrant, jewel-studded rice pilaf. This isn't just a recipe; it's an invitation to create a masterpiece that will captivate your senses and impress every guest.

## What is Lamb Ouzi?

Lamb Ouzi, also spelled "Ouzi" or "Qoozi," is a revered dish across many parts of the Middle East, particularly in countries like Iraq, Syria, Jordan, and Lebanon. At its heart, it’s a celebratory dish, often reserved for special occasions, large family gatherings, Eid al-Adha, or weddings. While variations exist, the essence of Lamb Ouzi lies in its combination of tender, spiced lamb and a rich, aromatic rice pilaf. The lamb can be prepared in various ways – sometimes stewed, sometimes roasted in large pieces – but the "Whole Slow Roasted" version is undoubtedly the most spectacular.

This grand presentation involves slow-roasting an entire lamb or a substantial cut, such as a leg or shoulder, until the meat is incredibly tender and easily pulls apart. The lamb is typically marinated in a blend of Middle Eastern spices, which not only tenderizes it further but also imbues it with layers of complex flavor. The accompanying rice is often cooked with lamb broth, mixed with ground lamb or beef, toasted nuts (almonds, pine nuts, pistachios), and sometimes dried fruits like raisins, creating a harmonious symphony of textures and tastes that perfectly complements the rich, savory lamb.

## Ingredients for Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi

Crafting this magnificent Lamb Ouzi requires a commitment to quality ingredients. Here's what you'll need to bring this Middle Eastern marvel to life:

For the Lamb:
*   1 whole young lamb (20-30 lbs) or a large lamb leg/shoulder (5-7 lbs)
*   Marinade:
    *   1/2 cup olive oil
    *   1/4 cup lemon juice
    *   1 head garlic, minced
    *   3-4 tbsp Ouzi spice blend (or a mix of: 1 tbsp each ground cumin, coriander, paprika; 1 tsp each black pepper, turmeric, allspice, cinnamon, cardamom; 1/2 tsp ground cloves)
    *   2 tbsp salt
    *   1 tbsp dried mint (optional)

For the Rice Pilaf:
*   3 cups basmati rice, rinsed until water runs clear
*   1 lb ground lamb or beef (optional, for mixing into rice)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   4 tbsp olive oil or ghee
*   6 cups lamb broth (or water + bouillon)
*   1 tbsp Ouzi spice blend (or a mix as above)
*   1 tsp salt
*   1/2 cup mixed nuts (pine nuts, slivered almonds, pistachios), lightly toasted
*   1/4 cup golden raisins (optional)
*   Fresh parsley or mint for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Lamb Ouzi

Preparing Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi is a labor of love, but the steps are straightforward and the reward is immense.

1.  **Prepare the Lamb:**
    *   Pat the lamb dry thoroughly. Using a sharp knife, make several deep incisions all over the lamb.
    *   In a bowl, combine all marinade ingredients. Rub the marinade generously all over the lamb, ensuring it penetrates the incisions. For best results, cover and refrigerate for at least 12 hours, preferably 24-48 hours.
    *   Bring the lamb to room temperature for about 2 hours before roasting.

2.  **Slow Roast the Lamb:**
    *   Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C).
    *   Place the lamb on a rack in a large roasting pan. Add 2-3 cups of water or broth to the bottom of the pan to keep the lamb moist and catch drippings.
    *   Cover the roasting pan tightly with foil, ensuring no steam escapes.
    *   Roast for 4-6 hours for a leg/shoulder, or 8-12 hours for a whole lamb, or until the internal temperature reaches 190-200°F (88-93°C) and the meat is fork-tender. Baste every 1-2 hours with the pan juices.
    *   For the last 30-45 minutes, remove the foil and increase the oven temperature to 375°F (190°C) to allow the skin to crisp up, if desired.
    *   Once cooked, remove the lamb from the oven, transfer it to a large carving board, and tent loosely with foil. Let it rest for at least 30-60 minutes before carving – this is crucial for juicy meat.

3.  **Prepare the Rice Pilaf:**
    *   While the lamb rests, prepare the rice. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat 2 tbsp olive oil/ghee over medium heat. Sauté the chopped onion until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
    *   If using ground meat, add it now and cook, breaking it up, until browned. Drain any excess fat.
    *   Add the rinsed basmati rice and toast for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly. This helps prevent sticking and enhances flavor.
    *   Stir in the Ouzi spice blend and salt. Pour in the lamb broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until all liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Do not lift the lid during this time.
    *   Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for another 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
    *   In a separate small pan, heat the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil/ghee. Add the mixed nuts and toast until lightly golden. Be careful not to burn them. If using, add the raisins for the last minute of toasting.
    *   Gently fold the toasted nuts and raisins into the cooked rice.

4.  **Assemble and Serve:**
    *   On a very large serving platter, spread the fragrant rice pilaf as a base.
    *   Carefully place the rested, carved, or shredded lamb on top of the rice.
    *   Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley or mint.
    *   Serve immediately with accompanying sauces and salads.

## Tips for Perfect Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi

Achieving a truly magnificent Lamb Ouzi requires attention to detail. Here are some tips to elevate your dish:

*   **Choose Wisely:** For a whole lamb, opt for a younger animal for more tender meat. For cuts, a bone-in leg or shoulder will yield the most flavor and moisture.
*   **Don't Skimp on Marination:** The longer the lamb marinates, the deeper the flavor will penetrate, and the more tender the meat will become. Overnight is good; 48 hours is fantastic.
*   **Low and Slow is Key:** Resist the urge to rush the roasting process. The low temperature and long cooking time are essential for breaking down tough fibers and rendering the meat incredibly tender and succulent.
*   **Rest Your Meat:** This is non-negotiable. Resting allows the juices to redistribute throughout the meat, ensuring every bite is moist and flavorful. Skipping this step will result in dry lamb.
*   **Moisture is Your Friend:** The water or broth in the bottom of the roasting pan creates a steamy environment, preventing the lamb from drying out. Replenish if it evaporates too quickly.
*   **Perfecting the Rice:** Rinsing the basmati rice thoroughly removes excess starch, preventing it from becoming sticky. Toasting the dry rice briefly before adding liquid also enhances its texture and nutty flavor.
*   **Taste and Adjust:** Always taste your marinade and rice seasoning. Adjust salt and spices as needed to suit your preference.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

Lamb Ouzi is a feast in itself, but it shines even brighter when surrounded by complementary dishes.

*   **Presentation:** Serve the whole roasted lamb or large pieces majestically atop a mound of the aromatic rice pilaf on a grand platter. Garnish generously with fresh herbs, extra toasted nuts, and perhaps some pomegranate seeds for a burst of color and tartness.
*   **Sauces:** Offer a side of traditional Arabic yogurt sauce (labneh with garlic and mint) or a simple tahini sauce. A fresh tomato-cucumber salad with lemon-mint dressing also provides a refreshing counterpoint.
*   **Salads:** Fattoush (a vibrant bread salad) or Tabbouleh (a finely chopped parsley and bulgur salad) are classic Middle Eastern companions that cut through the richness of the lamb.
*   **Vegetables:** Grilled or roasted vegetables like bell peppers, zucchini, or eggplant make excellent additions.
*   **Drinks:** Pair with a robust red wine (like a Syrah or Cabernet Sauvignon) or a refreshing non-alcoholic option like a mint lemonade or ayran (savory yogurt drink).

## Variations and Substitutions

While the traditional Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi is spectacular, there are ways to adapt it to your preferences and available ingredients:

*   **Lamb Cut:** If a whole lamb is too daunting, a bone-in leg of lamb or a lamb shoulder works beautifully. Cooking time will be significantly reduced, but the principle of low and slow remains. You can also use lamb shanks for individual servings, though this changes the "whole roasted" aspect.
*   **Rice Base:** While basmati is preferred for its aroma and separate grains, other long-grain white rices can be used. For a richer flavor, some recipes use a base of freekeh (roasted green wheat).
*   **Nut Medley:** Feel free to customize your nuts! Walnuts, cashews, or even pecans can be added or substituted. Always toast them for maximum flavor.
*   **Spice Blend:** If you can't find a pre-made Ouzi spice blend, you can create your own with individual spices like cumin, coriander, cinnamon, allspice, cardamom, black pepper, and a touch of nutmeg or cloves. Adjust ratios to your taste.
*   **Stuffing:** Some elaborate versions involve stuffing the lamb cavity with a part of the spiced rice pilaf before roasting, allowing the rice to absorb even more lamb juices.
*   **Vegetarian Option (for the rice):** While the lamb is central, the rice pilaf itself can be made vegetarian by omitting the ground meat and using vegetable broth, making it a delicious side dish for other meals.

Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi is more than just a recipe; it's a culinary journey, a testament to the rich flavors and generous spirit of Middle Eastern hospitality. Embark on this delicious adventure and create a meal that will be remembered long after the last bite.
